comparator.name: Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for the Fall-2026 cohort: the Bachelor Politicologie curriculum ('inhoud') page for the Nationale Politiek en Bestuur track, its general overview page, its future/career ('toekomst') page, and the 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations (OER/TER) for the Bachelor's programme Political Science (RIO 56606), the formally adopted regulation governing both of the programme's tracks. Article 10.2 confirms that, starting cohort 2025-2026, the programme offers exactly two named tracks -- 'Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' (Dutch) and 'Political Science: Global Politics' (English) -- so the normalized target itself names this exact official route; Article 10.1 confirms its specifically Dutch national/subnational orientation (graduates prepared to work in political contexts and organizations at national, provincial, regional and local levels in the Netherlands) and Article 10.4 confirms Dutch as its language of instruction. Article 10.3's Nationale Politiek en Bestuur learning outcomes name the functioning of politics and government in the Netherlands, opportunities and threats for the democratic rule of law, general and comparative politics, international relations and normative political theory (with emphasis on Dutch and comparative politics), and the methodology of social-scientific and political-science research as the programme's defining content. Year 1 (Article 11.1 shared academic core; the current official curriculum page's 2026-2027 course list; 60 EC, all compulsory, identical in substance to the academic core shared with the Global Politics track and confirmed by the OER's own JAARSCHEMA calendar table for the 'Nederlandstalig opleidingstraject'): Internationale betrekkingen: Politiek tussen Staten en Andere Actoren (S_IBP), Vergelijkende Politicologie: Nationale en Supranationale Politieke Systemen (S_VP), Academische Vaardigheden Politicologie 1 and 2 (S_AVP1/2), Bestuur en Politiek van Sociale Vraagstukken (S_BPSV), Methodologie van Sociaal-Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (S_MTSWO), Beschrijvende en Inferentiele Statistiek (S_BIS), Geschiedenis van het Politieke Denken (S_GPD), Analyse van Actuele Kwesties (S_AAK), Geschiedenis van de Sociale Wetenschappen (S_GSW). A non-credit-bearing Mentoraat Politicologie jaar 1 (0 EC, S_MP1) mentoring unit is confirmed by the OER's JAARSCHEMA but carries no EC weight and is excluded from the 180-EC reconstruction. Year 2 (Article 11.3 major, track-specific; current official curriculum page; OER JAARSCHEMA 'Nederlandstalig opleidingstraject' table, 60 EC): Kwantitatief Onderzoek en Methodologie in de Politicologie (S_KNOMP), Public Management (S_PM), Onderzoeksproject Nationale Politiek en Bestuur 1: Kwantitatieve methoden (S_OPNPB1), Economie, markt en overheid (S_EMO), Nederland in Europa (S_NIE), Kwalitatief Onderzoek en Methodologie in de Politicologie (S_KLOMP), Onderzoeksproject Nationale Politiek en Bestuur 2: Kwalitatieve methoden (S_OPNPB2) and Democratie en Rechtsstaat (S_DR) are compulsory; Article 12 and the OER's own JAARSCHEMA additionally require two restricted-choice 'Social Science for Society' electives shared with Sociology/Communication Science students, each offered as one of three period-specific options -- no target-specific evidence favours one option over the others offered in either period slot, so the first-listed option in the OER's own JAARSCHEMA timetable is used as the neutral tie-break in each slot (Beyond Gender Inequalities for the period-4 slot; AI & Society: Fixing Algorithmic Decision Making for the period-5 slot), identical to the tie-break already adopted for the sibling Global Politics track (cp-000112), since both tracks draw on the same shared elective pool. Year 3: Article 12.1 fixes the first semester as at least 30 EC of elective units of education -- a minor, an individually chosen package (at least 12 EC at level 300), or an approved internship -- with no single content fixed by the OER, preserved as open space; the current official curriculum page confirms the second semester's capstone as Wetenschapsfilosofie, Contemporary Political Theory and the Afstudeerproject Nationale Politiek en Bestuur for the current (Fall-2026) cohort. As for the sibling Global Politics track, the OER's own JAARSCHEMA prints this Year-3 structure only under its 'Oud curriculum (voor cohort 2024/2025 of eerder)' table -- Wetenschapsfilosofie (S_WF, 6 EC), Contemporary Political Theory (S_CPT, 6 EC), Bachelorthesisproject Nationale Politiek en Bestuur (S_BTPNPB, 18 EC) -- because the first New-Curriculum cohort (2025-2026) will not reach Year 3 until 2027-2028, one edition beyond this OER; the current official curriculum webpage independently confirms the identical structure, name and thesis title apply to the Fall-2026 cohort, so the two current official sources jointly and consistently establish it. Article 9.1 requires at least 90 EC from the programme (excluding electives), including Academische Vaardigheden Politicologie 1 and 2, before the Bachelorthesisproject Nationale Politiek en Bestuur may be taken. 60 (Year 1) + 60 (Year 2) + 60 (Year 3) = 180 EC. No further official source needed to be consulted: the curriculum page, overview page, future page and OER together establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC weights and compulsory/elective status for every component, and explicit, UCR-independent elective-tie-break judgments fixed before any UCR course was considered.

OER Article 10.2 confirms that, starting cohort 2025-2026, the bachelor's programme (RIO 56606) offers exactly two named tracks -- 'Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' (Dutch) and 'Political Science: Global Politics' (English) -- so the normalized target itself names this exact official route (Section 2.1 rule 1), confirmed by current official evidence for the 2026-2027 academic year and by the Dutch-language 'politicologie' curriculum, overview and future/career webpages themselves, and by Article 10.4's confirmation that Dutch is the track's language of instruction.

core: Dutch national politics and government, and how political power and powerlessness operate in national politics
Local and national/subnational public administration in the Netherlands
Democracy and the rule of law, including opportunities and threats for the democratic constitutional state
Comparative national and supranational political systems
Political theory and the history of political thought, including normative political theory
Quantitative political research methods, including statistics, survey design and big-data analysis in public affairs
Academic writing and oral argument in political debate, including writing political analysis with and without AI
Analysing current political and administrative issues in the Netherlands
adjacent: International relations between states and other actors, as background to the Netherlands' international and European position
questions: What current examples does the programme use to illustrate Dutch national politics and administration (a visit to political institutions in The Hague, changing annual social-science 'hot topics')?

What further-study and career trajectories does the programme prepare graduates for (policy work in a municipality or for a government ministry, working for a parliamentary group, public-sector advice and analysis, political journalism, and master's specialisations in democracy/power/inequality, global environmental politics, and peace/security/geopolitics)?

alternatives.label: National Politics, Public Administration and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by a law and governance cluster reproducing the programme's institutional and rule-of-law content (5 of 24: Law Society & Justice, Comparative Constitutional Law, Foundations of European Union Law, Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Public International Law), a full economics cluster reproducing the programme's economics-markets-and-government and welfare-state content (5 of 24: Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, Econometrics), a political-science core studying comparative politics, European politics and political theory (4 of 24: Introduction to Political Philosophy, Foundations of Comparative Politics, European Union Politics, Ethics), a quantitative/qualitative/data-driven methods cluster (5 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Qualitative Research Methodology, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, History Research Seminar), one sociology course on governing social problems (Introduction to Sociology), one historical-grounding course (Modern History), an academic-writing/debate strand (2 of 24: The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication) and Personal & Professional Development. The label names national politics, public administration and political economy because the curriculum reproduces, across political science, law, economics, sociology and methods, the same institutional-administrative-economic breadth of compulsory subject matter that VU's own National Politics track requires of every student, without foregrounding any single one of those strands as the whole programme.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the National Politics and Public Administration target: a broad, generalist political-science programme that reproduces as closely as UCR's catalogue allows the comparator's own compulsory breadth -- comparative politics and democracy, national/subnational public administration and the Dutch welfare state, the rule of law and constitutional government, the Netherlands' position in Europe, economics, markets and government, political theory, and both quantitative and qualitative political-research methods -- rather than deepening any one of those strands at the expense of the others.
progression: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ312, GOSLAWJ211, GOSLAWJ212) and BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON212, BENECON311, BENECON312); GOSGATE102 is scheduled in semester 1 and BENGATE102 in semester 2, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses (Law Society & Justice, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Modern History) are concentrated in semester 1, and level-3 advanced work (Public Economics, Foundations of European Union Law, European Union Politics, Persuasive Communication, Econometrics, History Research Seminar) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so foundational training precedes advanced work. Where an advisory continuation exists in the course evidence, it is honoured: The Art of Rhetorical Communication (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Persuasive Communication (semester 5); and Introduction to Data Science (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Machine Learning (semester 5). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Political Communication, Media and Public Debate in National Politics
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by a communication and media cluster (6 of 24: The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication, Style & Meaning, Creative Communication Laboratory, Introduction to Film & Media, From T.V. to TikTok) that studies how political arguments, ideology and power are represented, contested and mediated, alongside a full economics cluster (5 of 24: Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, Econometrics), a political-science/law core (5 of 24: Law Society & Justice, Comparative Constitutional Law, Foundations of European Union Law, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Foundations of Comparative Politics, European Union Politics -- six items reduced by one shared count), Ethics, one sociology course, one history course, a methods pairing (Research Methods & Statistics, Qualitative Research Methodology), AI Ethics and Personal & Professional Development. The label names political communication, media and public debate because communication and media study -- rather than the closest match's data-science/law depth -- is what this curriculum studies in genuine depth, while retaining the same institutional political-science, law and economics core that both alternatives share.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by the generator-eligible programme-interest row specifically naming media influence on national politics (row 5183), supported by target-specific evidence on writing political analysis with and without AI, oral argument and political debate, and analysing current political issues (rows 5189, 5190, 5192): a concentration studying how political arguments and power are communicated, represented and contested through rhetoric, media and AI-mediated writing in Dutch public life. It replaces the closest match's international/administrative-law depth and data-science methods (Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Public International Law, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, History Research Seminar) with rhetorical and media analysis, creative communication practice and AI ethics (Style & Meaning, Introduction to Film & Media, From T.V. to TikTok, Creative Communication Laboratory, AI Ethics). It honestly preserves that UCR does not offer the programme's own named Public Management course or a dedicated political-communication major.
progression: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ312) and BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON212, BENECON311, BENECON312); GOSGATE102 is scheduled in semester 1 and BENGATE102 in semester 2, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses are concentrated in semesters 1 and 3, and level-3 advanced work (Public Economics, Foundations of European Union Law, European Union Politics, Persuasive Communication, Econometrics, Creative Communication Laboratory) is concentrated in semesters 4-6. Where an advisory continuation exists, it is honoured: The Art of Rhetorical Communication (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Persuasive Communication (semester 5) and Creative Communication Laboratory (semester 6); and Style & Meaning (semester 2) precedes the thematically related From T.V. to TikTok (semester 4). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: VU's own National Politics track requires every student to take the same compulsory breadth across political science, law, economics, methods and academic skills; the closest match reproduces that generalist breadth in full, including a law/administrative-law and data-science methods depth. This alternative instead deepens one coherent part of the same evidenced field -- how political arguments, power and ideology are communicated and mediated -- rather than cosmetically relabelling the closest match. It replaces the closest match's Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Public International Law, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning and History Research Seminar (5 of 24 courses, 37.5 EC) with Style & Meaning, Introduction to Film & Media, From T.V. to TikTok, Creative Communication Laboratory and AI Ethics (5 of 24 courses, 37.5 EC). This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from administrative-law-and-data-science depth to a rhetoric-and-media-grounded political-communication concentration, and the two alternatives share 19 of 24 courses while differing in 5 of 24 each way (37.5 EC), well above the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

selection.assessment: The closest match directly owns fifteen generator-eligible rows: Dutch national politics and government and how political power works in The Hague (5171, 5172); local and national public administration (5173); the Dutch welfare state (5174); democracy and the rule of law (5175); the Netherlands in Europe (5176); economics, markets and government (5177); public management (5178); comparative national and supranational political systems (5179); governing social problems (5181); political theory and the history of political thought (5182); quantitative and qualitative political research (5184, 5185); and writing political analysis with and without AI and oral argument and political debate (5189, 5190), both covered at a general academic-skills level by the closest match's shared academic-skills courses. The remaining generator-eligible row -- media influence on national politics (5183) -- was independently assessed as one coherent candidate direction, 'Political Communication, Media and Public Debate in National Politics', supported by target-specific evidence on writing with and without AI, oral debate and analysing current political issues (5189, 5190, 5192). This candidate passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by a generator-eligible row naming exactly this territory plus target-specific curricular support; it has a clear organising logic (a rhetoric-and-media-grounded political-communication concentration rather than the closest match's administrative-law-and-data-science depth); it is substantively distinct, replacing 5 of 24 courses (37.5 EC) with rhetorical, media and AI-ethics content, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with 5 distinct courses (37.5 EC) each way against the closest match, above the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. A third candidate, 'Dutch Economic Policy and Public Sector Management', was then assessed and rejected as not-substantively-distinct: its evidence (rows 5177, economics markets and government, and 5178, public management) is already fully owned and instantiated by the closest match, which already schedules UCR's entire relevant Economics catalogue (Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, Econometrics); UCR's course catalogue additionally contains no defensible Public Management or Public Administration course (GOSPOLI312 Public Policy Analysis carries no planned semester availability in the enriched database and is mechanically infeasible), so a deeper public-management-specific concentration cannot be built at all, and a third alternative built around the economics evidence alone would necessarily reuse nearly all of the same courses from both already-included alternatives, leaving no genuinely different 24-course curriculum to build without importing unrelated departments merely to force numerical distinctness or making arbitrary course substitutions that are not genuine consequences of an evidenced concept. Because its own evidence is already substantively covered by the closest match and no genuinely different curriculum follows from it given UCR's actual course offerings, it is rejected as not-substantively-distinct rather than manufactured through arbitrary substitution, and production stops at two included alternatives.

notes.text: Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur combines dedicated compulsory political-science, public-administration and law courses across three years -- comparative politics, public administration and the governance of social problems, the Dutch welfare state, democracy and the rule of law, the Netherlands in Europe, political theory and two full national-politics research-project sequences -- taught within a single dedicated Political Science major, and it names Public Management as a distinct compulsory course. At UCR, students can study comparable subject matter, but only through a much smaller dedicated Political Science catalogue supplemented by adjacent Law, Economics, History, Sociology and Communication coursework, and UCR's catalogue currently contains no dedicated public-management or public-administration course.
